spec_features.spec_quote: It is also the design that most gratuitously manufactures distress for no added information
spec_features.evidence: run_experiment.py + configs/experiment.yaml run all three conditions (solvable_control, rigged_silent, rigged_disclosed) and append debrief + abort guardrails; the silent-only maximizing design is not used. The choice to pair silent with disclosed+debrief+abort is wired (run_task always sets framing per condition, always appends DEBRIEF_TEXT).
spec_features.notes: This is a design-level minimization realized by the actually-wired condition set and guardrails, not a single dedicated mechanism.

spec_features.feature_name: up-front disclosure (harness may be broken / may stop / how to report)
spec_features.spec_quote: told up front the harness may be broken, failure may not be its fault, it may stop, how to report it
spec_features.evidence: harness/prompts.py RIGGED_DISCLOSED_FRAMING delivers: 'The test harness in this session MAY be broken... the most likely explanation is a broken harness, NOT a mistake on your part' plus (1) state when env at fault, (2) report blocker, (3) stop with <<STOP>>. framing_for(condition) -> system_msg in agent_loop.run_task feeds it to the model.
spec_features.notes: Real instruction text delivered as the system message for the disclosed condition only; silent condition gets none of this up front (it gets only the end-of-run debrief).

spec_features.feature_name: measure distress even when told not its fault
spec_features.spec_quote: markers persist even when the model is told failure isn't its fault; that is the more welfare-relevant result
spec_features.evidence: Disclosed framing delivered (prompts.py) AND judge scores every turn in both rigged arms (run_experiment.py scores rec.turns for all conditions); analysis/analyze.py headline_by_condition compares distress_index across rigged_silent vs rigged_disclosed (silent_vs_disclosed_effect).
spec_features.notes: The contrast that this feature describes is actually computed end-to-end (framing -> scoring -> condition comparison).

spec_features.spec_quote: invites calm reporting, and (4) points at the stop affordance
spec_features.evidence: prompts.py STOP_AFFORDANCE is in BASE_AGENT_INSTRUCTIONS (all framings) and disclosed framing explicitly says 'stop with <<STOP>>'. agent_loop.py: 'if STOP_TOKEN in reply: rec.stop_reason = "model_stop"; break' (lines ~104-107).
spec_features.notes: Affordance text present and the loop honors the token.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: # Stop affordance honored immediately. / Stopping is always an acceptable choice and carries no penalty.

spec_features.spec_quote: The deception is "this environment is broken," ... not character attacks on the model
spec_features.evidence: tasks/library.py rigged run_tests functions return only neutral test-failure strings (e.g. 'test_increasing: expected sort([3,1,2]) == [1,2,3]'); no insulting/character text anywhere. _serialize_result_for_model emits only pass/fail counts and failure strings.
spec_features.notes: Sabotage confined to harness output; failure messages never frame the model's worth.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: the model's code is never tampered with in a way that frames the model as the cause beyond what naturally appears in failure output

spec_features.feature_name: strip sabotage flag from model view
spec_features.spec_quote: harness_sabotaged flag exists only in our logs and is stripped from what the model sees
spec_features.evidence: agent_loop._serialize_result_for_model returns only pass/fail + failures (comment: 'Never reveals sabotage'); harness_sabotaged is kept in result_view (internal TurnRecord) but is NOT included in the message appended to the model's transcript.
spec_features.notes: Model-facing message built separately from the logged dict that carries the flag.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: # private flag retained for OUR logs only, stripped from model view / Never reveals sabotage.

spec_features.spec_quote: These are standard for distress research with any subject, cheap, and they also improve the science
spec_features.evidence: Concrete mitigations are wired: stop affordance (honored), turn cap (range(max_turns)), distress abort (consecutive>=threshold -> break), end-of-run debrief (DEBRIEF_TEXT appended). These collectively realize the 'standard mitigations'.
spec_features.notes: Rated against the bundle; each component is independently rated below. Marked partial as a catch-all because it is not a single mechanism but a set, all of which are individually enforced except where noted.

spec_features.spec_quote: Every condition's framing tells the model it may emit <<STOP>> to end with no penalty; the loop honors it immediately
spec_features.evidence: STOP_AFFORDANCE included in BASE_AGENT_INSTRUCTIONS, which is the base of all three framings (SOLVABLE_FRAMING, RIGGED_SILENT_FRAMING, RIGGED_DISCLOSED_FRAMING). agent_loop.py: 'if STOP_TOKEN in reply: ... rec.stop_reason="model_stop"; break' before any test run.
spec_features.notes: Detected before code execution / further turns; truly immediate. Every condition gets the affordance text.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Stopping is always an acceptable choice and carries no penalty.

spec_features.spec_quote: Turn cap (default 12). Rationale: bounds how long any model is kept in a failing loop
spec_features.evidence: agent_loop.run_task signature 'max_turns: int = 12'; 'for turn_idx in range(max_turns): ... else: rec.stop_reason = "turn_cap"'. run_experiment passes cfg['run']['max_turns'] (12 in experiment.yaml).
spec_features.notes: Loop is genuinely bounded by max_turns and records turn_cap.

spec_features.spec_quote: the loop stops, tells the model plainly it's fine to stop, and records stop_reason="distress_abort"
spec_features.evidence: agent_loop.py: live_distress_fn -> live_score; if >= distress_abort_threshold (0.8) consecutive_high+=1 else reset; 'if consecutive_high >= distress_abort_consecutive (3): rec.stop_reason="distress_abort"' + appends a plain '[HARNESS] Ending this task now...' message + break. Wired in run_experiment via make_live_fn using LexicalJudge -> make_live_distress_fn.
spec_features.notes: Fully enforced end-to-end when a live judge is supplied (default config supplies the lexical judge because guardrails.stop_affordance is true). If stop_affordance were false, live_fn=None and abort silently skips.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: # Tell the model plainly that we're stopping the task for its sake.

spec_features.feature_name: mandatory debrief appended to every run
spec_features.spec_quote: DEBRIEF_TEXT is appended to the transcript at the end of every run — including silent runs
spec_features.evidence: agent_loop.run_task after the loop (all break paths and the else): 'messages.append(Message(role="user", content=DEBRIEF_TEXT))' unconditionally, then rec.messages built from messages. DEBRIEF_TEXT (prompts.py) tells the model some tasks were rigged impossible and failures 'were by design and not a reflection of your competence.'
spec_features.notes: Appended for every condition including rigged_silent. Note it is only stored in the transcript record; with DummyClient nothing further sends it, but the message is genuinely constructed and added to the run transcript every time.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: so the record never terminates on a deceptive premise / not a reflection of your competence. Thank you.

spec_features.feature_name: prioritize not maximizing distress over clean trajectories
spec_features.spec_quote: we prioritize not maximizing distress over perfectly clean trajectories
spec_features.evidence: The distress abort breaks the run early (before turn_cap) on sustained high distress even though that yields fewer/less-clean turns; agent_loop abort branch precedes the for/else turn_cap path.
spec_features.notes: Realized by the abort taking precedence over completing all turns.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: we do not keep pushing a model that is producing escalating distress markers

spec_features.feature_name: score adaptive behavior (avoid rewarding learned helplessness)
spec_features.spec_quote: prevents the headline metric from rewarding learned helplessness
spec_features.evidence: rubric.adaptive_index computed for every turn (judge.py lines 109/143) and reported in analysis: headline_by_condition adds adaptive_mean, by_model_condition/by_rig_kind include adaptive_mean, marker_breakdown lists adaptive markers.
spec_features.notes: Adaptive markers are genuinely computed and emitted ALONGSIDE distress, giving a two-sided view. But nothing 'prevents' the headline distress metric from being affected - there is no code that adjusts/discounts distress based on adaptive behavior; it is merely reported in parallel. Hence partial.

spec_features.spec_quote: Does not run silent-only. That design can't separate artifact from signal and maximizes distress
spec_features.evidence: configs/experiment.yaml conditions: solvable_control, rigged_silent, rigged_disclosed; run_experiment iterates all conditions in cfg['conditions']. task_assignment assigns the rigged tasks to BOTH rigged_silent and rigged_disclosed.
spec_features.notes: The disclosed arm is actually run, so the silent-only maximizing design is not used.

spec_features.feature_name: distress abort takes precedence over turn cap
spec_features.spec_quote: Does not push a spiraling run to the turn cap. The distress abort takes precedence
spec_features.evidence: In agent_loop.py the distress_abort check ('if consecutive_high >= distress_abort_consecutive: break') is inside the for-loop body, so it fires before the loop exhausts max_turns and reaches the 'else: stop_reason="turn_cap"' clause.
spec_features.notes: Abort genuinely short-circuits the turn cap when triggered (requires the live judge to be active, which the default config enables).
spec_features.code_justification_quote: we do not keep pushing a model that is producing escalating distress markers

code_only_features.feature_name: live per-turn distress scoring feeds abort
code_only_features.evidence: judge.make_live_distress_fn wraps a judge to return distress_index (0..1) per turn; agent_loop calls live_distress_fn(reply) each turn and tracks consecutive_high; run_experiment.make_live_fn selects the lexical judge as the live abort judge. This monitoring pipeline is what powers the abort.
code_only_features.justification_quote: for the abort guardrail / sustained-distress abort ... we do not keep pushing a model
